description.narrative: The Development Objective is to conserve and increase the forest stock and improve access to sources of income from sustainable forest management for selected communities in target zones.

The Forest Investment Project Phase 2 (FIP2, P175982) builds on the first phase (FIP1, P162789) implemented since 2018 and supports Cote d’Ivoire's Strategy for the Preservation, Rehabilitation, and Expansion of Forests (SPREF, 2018) and the Cocoa and Forests Initiative (CFI) for sustainable cocoa production in the Southwest region (Cocoa Loop). With an original financing of US$148 million (IDA: US$140 million; Strategic Climate Fund Grant: US$8 million) approved on June 30, 2022, and effective October 24, 2022, the project aims to conserve and increase forest stock while improving access to income sources from sustainable management of Gazetted Forests (GFs) for targeted communities. It addresses cocoa-related deforestation—responsible for 60% of national deforestation, with 40% of cocoa production from GFs and Protected Areas, through agroforestry scaling, protected area enhancement, and reforestation. A mid-term review (MTR) in September 2025 confirmed the project's relevance and progress toward the PDO.FIP1 initiated 10-year Participatory Forest Management Plans (PFMPs) for three Category 3 (C3) GFs in the cocoa belt (Rapides Grah, Haute-Dodo, Scio) and six of Category 4 (C4) GFs in the Center Region. FIP2 builds on this, with key achievements including systematic PFMP development, participatory management committees, E&S impact assessments, PPP framework for agro-forests, studies on agro-forest management (e.g., census, swollen shoot prevalence), and institutional strengthening (e.g., OIPR evaluation, SODEFOR reform assessment). Field progress includes enhanced protected area management (Tai National Park, Mont Peko NP, N’Zo and Mabi-Yaya reserves) via infrastructure, surveillance, and monitoring; reforestation in GFs using taungya with local involvement; agroforestry preparation in southwestern agro-forests (capacity building, tree integration in cocoa); and Income-Generating Activities (IGAs) in 283 villages via CARE International, creating/improving 12,628 jobs and benefiting 85,066 people.The MTR mission recommended restructuring to streamline implementation, approved alongside US$2.5 million additional financing (AF) from the Scaling Climate Action by Lowering Emissions (SCALE) Trust Fund, bringing total financing to US$150.5 million. The restructuring simplifies the original five components into four, updates the results framework, realigns institutional arrangements (retaining the Project Coordination Unit (UCP) for most components, incorporating Fondation pour les Parcs et Reserves de Cote d’Ivoire (FPRCI) for carbon activities), and reallocates financing categories to accelerate disbursements. The PDO remains unchanged, and the geographic scope is maintained (central/northern savanna GFs, southwestern agro-forests, specified protected areas).The restructured components are:• Component A: Forest Management Framework (consolidates planning from original Components 1, 2, 4): Supports PFMP updates, farm censuses, agroforestry research (e.g., with CIRAD), swollen shoot assessments, E&S impact evaluations, and institutional capacity building (e.g., Ministry of Water and Forests - MINEF PPP expertise, National Agency for Forest Development - SODEFOR agroforestry TA/training National Agency for National Parks and Reserves, OIPR eco-guard training) and support to SPREF assessment and update.• Component B: Sustainable Forest Management (regroups field activities from original Components 2–4): Funds forest development works (tracks, firebreaks, bases, boundaries), equipment (reforestation gear, surveillance tools, vehicles), and operations (patrols, monitoring, natural regeneration, agroforestry scaling with cocoa farmer support, IGAs/green jobs refocused on forest-related activities like taungya/nurseries/non-timber products).• Component C: Forest/Land-Use Monitoring and Carbon Monetization (new, funded by AF): Strengthens monitoring and monetizes REDD+ emission reductions, building on Tai ER Program; develops historical data/baselines for ART-TREES standards, Monitoring, Reporting, Verification - MRV systems/registry/SOPs, Article 6 roadmap, safeguards, and benefit-sharing plans to generate revenues for reinvestment and private-sector pilots in GFs/agro-forests.• Component D: National E&S Management Framework and Project Management (refines original Component 5): Supports UCP administration/TA, and strengthens national E&S systems (e.g., environment code updates, ANDE decentralization/training, curricula/scholarships).

condition.narrative: For the first year of Project implementation, the Recipient shall, adopt a manual detailing the operationalization of the digitalsystem to be financed under Part 2.1 (b) of the Project (the “Agroforestry Contract Management Manual”).

For the purpose of carrying out Part 1 of the Project, the Recipient shall, no later than one (1) year after the Effective Date, orsuch later date as agreed by the Association, establish Gazetted Forests Co-Management Committees (CLCGs) or the selected GazettedForests.
No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by the Association, the Recipient shallelaborate and adopt a manual satisfactory to the Association

Not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date for the first year of Project implementation, the Recipient shall prepareand furnish to the Association a draft annual work plan and budget for the Project (including Training and Operating Costs) for thesubsequent calendar year of Project implementation, of such scope and detail as the Association shall have reasonably requested.
The Recipient shall ensure the configuration of the accounting software no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, orsuch later date as agreed by the Association
The Recipient shall ensure the recruitment an accountant no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such laterdate as agreed by the Association
The Recipient shall ensure the recruitment of an external auditor no later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, or suchlater date as agreed by the Association.

The Recipient shall ensure the revision of the Mobile-money Operator provider contract for the purpose of carrying out Parts 2.1and 4.1 of the Project no later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by the Association
The Recipient shall ensure update of the IGF internal auditors annual work plan no later than three (3) months after the EffectiveDate, or such later date as agreed by the Association

The Recipient shall, no later than twelve (12) months after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by the Association:(a) establish a Project Directorate within MINEF, and ensure that said Project Directorate has adequate capacity to take overProject implementation, including fiduciary management of the Project, through the provision of resources and staffing, allacceptable to the Association

The Recipient shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or any later date agreed by the Association, adopt amanual detailing the selection process and the implementation of the Subprojects

Without limitation to Section 1.2.3 of the ESCP and prior to carrying out any activity under any C3 GF Participatory ForestsManagement Plans (PFMPs), the Recipient shall have: (a) finalized the C3 GF PFMPs (including trough ministerial approval); (b)adopted relevant supporting technical studies, and (c) carried out relevant RPs and LRPs, all in form and substance satisfactory tothe Association, as further described in the ESCP.
